title: Unsloth Shrinks MiniMax's 428B M3.1 Flash Model to Run Locally on 150GB RAM
summary:
Unsloth released 2-bit dynamic GGUF quantizations of MiniMax's 428B parameter M3.1 Flash model that reduce its footprint by 45% to 143.9GB and allow it to run locally on 150GB of RAM. The compressed version retains 91.5% top 1 token accuracy across seven domains and works with Unsloth Desktop and llama.cpp, while a smaller UD-IQ1_M quantization retains about 89.9% top 1 accuracy.

Independent evaluations also showed lower coding benchmark results than MiniMax reported for the model. While MiniMax claims M3.1 Flash scores 38 on Terminal-Bench 4.0, two outside tests recorded a score of 26, including a 25.2% mark from evaluator Vals AI that still topped the 1% solved by its predecessor M3. Vals AI noted that M3.1 Flash generated roughly 15 times as many output tokens as M3 on tax and legal tasks to achieve its higher accuracy.

The local quantizations follow MiniMax's Oct. 23 release of open weights for M3.1 Flash, a mixture-of-experts model that activates 23B parameters per token and uses NVFP4 for MoE layers alongside BF16 and MXFP8 for the remaining weights.

The biggest improvement came on Terminal-Bench 4. M3 only solved 1% of tasks, while M3.1-Flash reached 25.2%, climbing from #47 to #22 overall and from #17 to #8 among open-weight models.

This is a substantial change in its ability to handle complex coding tasks.

selectedTweets.bestBit: On Tax Agent and Legal Research, it generated roughly 15 times as many output tokens as M3, most of them devoted to reasoning.
selectedTweets.text:
One notable change is how much longer M3.1-Flash reasons through problems. On Tax Agent and Legal Research, it generated roughly 15 times as many output tokens as M3, most of them devoted to reasoning.

That additional reasoning likely explains part of the improvement. M3.1-Flash is solving substantially more problems, but it's also spending far more tokens attempting them. The gains in accuracy shouldn't be confused with gains in efficiency.
